chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Wehnwood Beach and the first Decca sessions
summary: After the Pearl the band played Wehnwood Beach and Fairyland, then recorded for Decca in New York every day for weeks; she wrote about twenty tunes in a week.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Going back again, when the band first went to Kansas City and you settled down there and you weren't playing with the band, what did you do?

After the Pearl Theatre and the Brunswick recordings we went back to Kansas City with me - I mean I was with them then, after the Pearl Theatre. So we went into the Wehnwood Beach there for that summer, I guess about 3 or 4 months or so. Then after that we came back to New York to record for Decca. I think we went in two Wehnwood Beach around '31 or '32, I'm sure. During that period before we came back to New York to record for Decca we played Fairyland - Wehnwood Beach, Fairyland, and places like that. The band began to rise after that, because we came back to New York to record for Decca and we recorded every day for 2 or 3 weeks. They just kept me in a hotel, somebody'd bring me sandwiches. I wrote 20 things in one week. They were all hits.
